'''官位相当制'''（かんいそうとうせい）とは、[[日本]]の[[律令制]]において、[[官人]]に付与する[[位階]]と[[官職]]との間に一定の相当関係を設定した官僚序列システム。
== 概要 == 日本律令の官位制は[[大宝律令|大宝令]]、[[養老令]]いずれも[[官位令]]において規定されているが、この模範となったのが[[唐]]官品令である。両者とも位階（唐では品階）と官職との対応関係を定めているが、その根本原則においては大きな差異があった。
唐律令制では、官人の序列を決定するのは官職という原則が通底しており、品階は官職の等級を表す指標に過ぎなかった。官人には官職とそれに対応する品階が与えられる建前であったが、実際の官職には限りがあったため、名目だけの官職があてがわれたり、[[散位]]（品階のみで官職を持たないこと）となる者も少なくなく、実質を持つ官職を得ることでようやく官僚序列の中に参加することができたのである。ここでは品階は大きな意味を持たず、官職のみが官僚機構の中で序列機能を果たしていた。
一方、日本律令制では、官人はまず位階によって序列化され、そして位階に応じた官職が与えられることとされていた。日本では律令制定以前から氏族制的序列が存在していたため、律令導入時に官人制を布く際、従前の序列を温存しながら各氏族を官人として再編成する必要に迫られた。これにより、日本では唐とは異なり、位階を主として官職を従とする官位制が導入されたのだと考えられている。この日本独特の官位制度を官位相当制という。
具体的には、官位令に基づいて位階ごとに就任可能な官職が厳密に定められていた。あくまでも位階が序列の主座にあったのであり、ある官職で実績・評価を重ねたとしても、唐のように官職の昇進を受けるのではなく、まず位階の昇進を受けて、その後に昇進後の位階に相当する官職の就任資格を得るのが原則であった。
なお、日本の官位呼称の制式では、官職と位階が相当である場合、官職を前に位階を後に記した（例:出羽守従五位下）。ただし、様々な事情により位階と官職の相当関係が成立していない事例も発生した。その場合、位階が高い場合は位階を先に記して「行」の文字を添え、後に官職を記した（例:従四位下行伊予守）。逆に官職が位階より上位である場合、同様に位階を先に記して「守」文字を添え、後に官職を記した（例:従五位下守右京大夫）。
実際の運用では、高い位階が全体的に与えられる傾向が強かった。また、時代が下り律令制の衰微とともに[[正六位]]よりも下の位階の叙任例はほとんどなくなっていった。
== 官位相当表 == === 養老令 === {{官位相当表 (養老令1)}} {{官位相当表 (養老令2)}} === 令外官 === {{官位相当表 (日本の令外官)}}
== 参考文献 == * 大隅清陽 「官位相当制」 『日本史大事典 2』 平凡社、1995。
== 関連項目 == * [[律令制]] * [[科挙]] * [[進士 (日本)]] * [[官位]] * [[日本の官制]] * [[准位]] - 官位相当制の対象外である[[宮人]]（[[女官]]）を対象とした官位相当に代わる制度
{{Japanese-history-stub}}

{{afc comment|1=see [[every:Kan'i sōtō system]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs}}

{{afc comment|1=see [[every:Kan'i sōtō system]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|12=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|12=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|12=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|12=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|12=draft}}

{{afc comment|1=see [[every:Kan'i sōtō system]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft|12=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft|12=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|12=draft|12=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|12=draft|12=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=draft|12=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=draft|12=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|12=draft|12=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=draft|12=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=draft|12=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=draft|12=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|12=draft|12=draft}}

{{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|12=draft|12=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft|12=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|12=draft|12=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|12=draft|12=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=draft|12=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=draft|12=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|12=draft|12=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=draft|12=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=draft|12=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=draft|12=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=draft|12=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|12=draft|12=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|12=draft|12=draft}}

{{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

{{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

{{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ritsuryō system|qq=}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanshoku|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taihō Code|qq=}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang dynasty|qq=}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|qq=}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Council of State|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-kan|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Central Affairs|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Center|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Rites|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikibu-shō|qq=}}

{{afc comment|1=This page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ritsuryō system|qq=}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanshoku|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taihō Code|qq=}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang dynasty|qq=}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|qq=}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Council of State|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-kan|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Central Affairs|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Center|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Rites|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikibu-shō|qq=}}

{{afc comment|1=This page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ritsuryō system|qq=}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks of Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanshoku|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taihō Code|qq=}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang dynasty|qq=}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|qq=}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Council of State|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-kan|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Central Affairs|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Center|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Rites|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikibu-shō|qq=}}

{{afc comment|1=This page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in {{ill|Japan|ja|日本|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ritsuryō system|qq=}}. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanshoku|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the {{ill|Taihō Code|ja|大宝律令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taihō Code|qq=}} and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=}}, specifically in the {{ill|Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang dynasty|qq=}}'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=}} |- !{{ill|Department of Divinities|ja|神祇官|1=Department of Divinities|blank=|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|13=User:Immanuelle/Department of Divinities|qq=}}!!{{ill|Great Council of State|ja|太政官|1=Daijō-kan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Council of State|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō-kan|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Central Affairs|ja|中務省|1=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Central Affairs|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Center|qq=}}!!{{ill|Ministry of Rites|ja|式部省|1=Shikibu-shō|lt=Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Rites|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikibu-shō|qq=}}
