It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|Kanshoku|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanshoku|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|qq=|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|qq=|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|qq=|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Kan'i sōtō system]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Kan'i sōtō system|Kan'i sōtō system]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kan'i Sōtōsei''' (官位相当制) refers to the bureaucratic Ranking system in [[:en:Japan|Japan]]'s [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]]. It established a fixed relationship between the {{ill|Court Ranks in Japan|ja|位階|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Court Ranks of Japan|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (court Ranks) and {{ill|East Asian government position|ja|官職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/East Asian government position|qq=}} (official posts) granted to officials. == Overview == The Japanese ritsuryō system's Rank-and-office structure was codified in the [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] and {{ill|Yōrō Code|ja|養老令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yōrō Code|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 養老律令|1=Yōrō Code|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2575743}}, specifically in the {{ill|Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Official Rank Ordinance|lt=Kan'irei|ja|官位令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan'irei|qq=}}. These codes were modeled after the [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]]'s "Guanpinling" (官品令). While both systems defined correspondences between Ranks (品階 in Tang) and offices, their foundational principles diverged significantly. In the Tang ritsuryō system, the principle of determining officials' hierarchies prioritized offices over Ranks. Ranks served merely as indicators of office grades. While officials were nominally assigned corresponding Ranks and offices, actual office positions were limited, leading to nominal office assignments or the designation of {{ill|San'i|ja|散位|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'i|qq=}} (officials holding Rank without office). Only upon receiving a substantive office could officials fully integrate into the bureaucratic hierarchy. Thus, Ranks held little intrinsic significance, with offices exclusively fulfilling hierarchical functions within the bureaucracy. Conversely, Japan's ritsuryō system first established officials' hierarchies through Ranks and then assigned offices corresponding to those Ranks. Before the ritsuryō system's introduction, Japan had an existing clan-based social order. When implementing the system, it was necessary to preserve traditional hierarchies while reorganizing clans into officials. Consequently, Japan adopted a unique system that prioritized Ranks over offices, known as "Kan'i Sōtōsei" (官位相当制). Under this system, offices eligible for each Rank were strictly defined in the Kan'irei. Since Ranks primarily determined officials' hierarchies, promotions were processed through Rank advancements rather than office-based achievements. Only after a Rank promotion could officials qualify for offices corresponding to their new Rank. In Japanese official titles, when Ranks and offices were aligned, the office preceded the Rank (e.g., 出羽守従五位下, "Governor of Dewa, Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade"). When discrepancies occurred, if the Rank was higher, it preceded the office with the addition of "行" (e.g., 従四位下行伊予守, "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Grade, Acting Governor of Iyo"). Conversely, when the office was higher, the Rank preceded the office with the addition of "守" (e.g., 従五位下守右京大夫, "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Provisional Minister of the Right Capital District"). In practice, higher Ranks were often granted more broadly. Over time, as the ritsuryō system declined, Ranks below {{ill|Shōroku-i|ja|正六位|1=Senior Sixth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|qq=}} were rarely awarded. ==Table== {{right|{{Tnavbar|Official Rank Equivalence Table (Yōrō Code 1)|mini=1}}}} {| class="wikitable" style="margin:0 0 0.5em 1.5em; text-align:center; font-size:90%; " !colspan="2" rowspan="2"| !!colspan="2"|{{ill|Officials|ja|官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Officials|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官吏|1=government official|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8985067}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Ministries|ja|日本の官制|1=structure of the ritsuryō government|lt=Eight Ministries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministries|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese administrative system#Eight Ministries|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8193883}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Positions|ja|職 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Positions|1=shiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11611224}}!!colspan="2"|{{ill|Bureaus|ja|寮 (律令制)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureaus|1=ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11457645}}!!colspan="5"|{{ill|Offices|ja|司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offices|1=shi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11412232}} |- ![[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]]!![[:en:Daijō-kan|Daijō-kan]]!![[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]]!![[:en:Shikibu-shō|Ministry of Ceremonial Affairs]]
